o eight (8) 35-gallon boxes per monthly pickup and one (1) additional high-volume pickup per contract year. Estimated annual utilization: up to 104 35-gallon boxes per contract year, calculated as up to eight (8) boxes per pickup multiplied by thirteen (13) pickups per year. The annual fixed price shall include the secure exterior storage cabinet, routine monthly pickups, one additional pickup per contract year, transportation, treatment/disposal, manifests, and disposal documentation. 7.0 Performance Requirements 8.0 Contractor Qualifications and Local Authorization The Contractor shall possess and maintain all licenses, permits, approvals, insurance, equipment, trained personnel, and disposal arrangements necessary to perform regulated medical waste collection, transport, treatment, and disposal. Before award, and upon request during performance, the Contractor shall provide written evidence that it is legally authorized to provide compensated regulated medical waste service at 3750 Chemawa Road NE, Salem, Oregon 97305. Evidence may include a City or County franchise, limited franchise, exemption, approved subcontract authorization, or other written local authority applicable to this location. The Contractor shall not represent that it can provide service at the location unless it can l

with the designated Government point of contact. Contractor personnel shall coordinate access with designated facility staff before each service call. The facility is closed during evenings and weekends unless access is specifically arranged in advance. 10.0 Government Furnished Property, Equipment, and Information The Government will not furnish equipment. The Government will provide access to the service location and will identify a facility point of contact for scheduling and acceptance. The SealingTech DCO Kit has been specifically engineered to integrate with existing Marine Corps cyber infrastructure and support operational testing requirements. Introducing alternate hardware platforms would require significant engineering analysis, configuration changes, compatibility testing, operator retraining, and validation activities while increasing technical and schedule risk. The Government determined that no other manufacturer provides a commercially available hardware solution that replicates the current Program-of-Record configuration while maintaining interoperability with fielded Marine Corps DCO systems. Accordingly, restricting this procurement to Sealing Technologies LLC is necessary to maintain mission readiness, ensure operational compatibility, and minimize lifecycle risk. sla_onsite.text: onID="2.0.2">CRITERION.EXCLUSION.CONVICTIONS.PARTICIPATION_IN_CRIMINAL_ORGANISATION</cbc:CriterionTypeCode> <cbc:Name>Osalemine kuritegelikus organisatsioonis</cbc:Name> <cbc:Description languageID="ET">Kas ettevõtja ise või tema haldus-, juht- või järelevalveorgani liige või isik, kellel on volitused seda ettevõtjat esindada, tema nimel otsuseid teha või teda kontrollida, on lõpliku süüdimõistva kohtuotsusega süüdi mõistetud kuritegelikus organisatsioonis osalemise eest kõige rohkem viimase viie aasta jooksul või kehtib süüdimõistvas kohtuotsuses sätestatud kõrvalejäämise kohustus endiselt?</cbc:Description> <cac:Legislation> <cbc:ID schemeID="CriteriaTaxonomy" schemeAgencyID="EU-COM-GROW" schemeVersionID="2.0.2">c753a2c5-59e6-4970-b6eb-27224e96bf76</cbc:ID> <cbc:Title languageID="ET">RHS § 95 lg 1 p 1 "keda või kelle haldus-, juhtimis- või järelevalveorgani liiget, prokuristi või muud isikut, kellel on volitus seda ettevõtjat esindada, tema nimel otsuseid teha või teda kontrollida, on karistatud kuritegelikus ühenduses osalemise eest". Kui hankemenetlusest kõrvaldamise alus esineb, võib ettevõtja soovi korral esitada tõendeid selle kohta, et ta on võtnud meetmeid oma usaldusväärsuse taastamiseks. Heastamise võimalus on ettevõtjal juh

Background: Sulphur Bank Mercury Mine (SBMM) is a 160-acre former cinnabar mercury mining site located on the eastern shore of the Oaks Arm of Clear Lake, approximately 70 miles northwest of Sacramento in Lake County, California. The mine operated from 1865 to 1957, utilizing both underground and open pit mining technologies. SBMM consists of mine tailings and waste rock and a flooded open pit mine (the Herman Impoundment). Approximately two million cubic yards of waste rock and low-grade ore remain onsite and contain high levels of mercury, arsenic and antimony. The Herman Impoundment is filled with water to a depth of 90 feet and is located approximately 750 feet east of Clear Lake, which is separated from the impoundment by an earthen dam composed of waste rock material and in-place bedrock. SBMM was placed on the Superfund National Priorities List (NPL) in August 1990 due to the impact of site contamination on the residents near the mine and wildlife in the vicinity of Clear Lake. The Elem Indian Colony (EIC) utilizes the land on and near SBMM for traditional cultural activities. Clear Lake is the source of drinking water for approx

for the development of the design and therefore is uniquely qualified to provide that service. EA is uniquely qualified to provide the site-specific subject matter expertise to meet U.S. EPA’s urgent time needs for overseeing implementation of the residential design in order to complete the remediation of the affected residential units at the Sulphur Bank Mine site. The SBMM site results in uncontrolled exposure to site-related contaminants for multiple user groups. This exposure results in unacceptable risk greatly exceeding EPA’s risk management range. This risk is greatest for the residents nearest the mine who live continuously on site-impacted soils. EPA needs to urgently move forward with the implementation of the design prepared by EA under task order 68HE0924F0079. The only alternative to employing the engineer of record who prepared the design would be to transfer responsibility for oversight to an external engineering firm. This would require month-long reviews, verification, and possible revision before being re-stamped by a new engineer of record. Such a takeover of the design would result in unacceptable delays, extending the period during which the affected community is exposed to harmful levels of site-related contamination. GENERAL INFORMATION This Scope of Work (SOW) establishes requirements for electrical inspection and repair services at the National Parks of Boston (BOST), including Charlestown Navy Yard, Bunker Hill Monument, and Dorchester Heights, under a Time and Materials (T&M) contract structure. The National Park Service (NPS) reserves the right to purchase materials directly to reduce costs when applicable. There is no limit on the number of site visits. All work requires a written quote submitted by the awardee and approved in writing by the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) before any work is performed. Materials procured by the contractor are subject to a maximum 20% markup, and all receipts must be provided to document compliance. 2. BACKGROUND The National Park Service requires electrical system inspection and repair services for twenty (20) buildings and associated grounds within the National Parks of Boston, located primarily at the Charlestown Navy Yard with additional sites at Bunker Hill Monument and Dorchester Heights. These historic structures range in age from approxi

se The selected contractor shall furnish all labor, transportation, equipment, tools, and supervision necessary to perform electrical system inspections and repairs at The National Parks of Boston on a Time and Materials basis. The NPS reserves the right to procure and supply materials directly where cost savings can be achieved; in such cases, contractor-supplied materials are not required, and no markup is applicable to Government-Furnished Materials (GFM). This contract is structured as a Base Year with two (2) subsequent Option Years. Each option year is subject to the Government's determination of satisfactory contractor performance and availability of appropriated funds. 3.2 Contract Line Item Structure This contract contains a single Time and Materials (T&M) Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) per contract year. There are no Firm Fixed Price CLINs. All work — including inspections, repairs, emergency response, and all other electrical services — is performed and billed under T&M pricing at the approved fully burdened labor rates. The contract ceiling for each year applies to the aggregate of all work performed at all locations during that period of performance.
